participants.label: Hub page
participants.note: The browser adds the page's real origin to what gets signed, so a look-alike site cannot get a usable signature.

participants.label: Authenticator
participants.note: Touch ID / Windows Hello / phone / security key. Holds the private key; the fingerprint only unlocks it locally and is never sent anywhere.

participants.label: AccessKey store
participants.note: Planned: flowpad/hub/builtin/access_key.py + flowpad/hub/app/services/access_keys.py. One AccessKey row per key, part of its user: kind (passkey today), credential id, public key, algorithm, sign count, backup flags, label. No secret in it.

participants.label: Verifier
participants.note: Whoever protects something: a hub action, or a machine checking an approval itself. Uses one shared verify function.

messages.label: Add access key
messages.note: Part 1 - register, once per passkey. The first key also needs a code emailed to the account; a later one needs a confirmation with an existing key.

messages.label: challenge, rp id, user id
messages.note: Challenge: random, signed by the hub, valid 5 minutes. rp id: the hub's domain. userVerification: required. Algorithms: ES256, RS256. Attestation: none.

messages.label: Fingerprint
messages.note: Matched on the device against the template stored in its secure chip. Only yes or no comes out.

messages.label: Create key pair
messages.note: A new pair for this rp id only. The private key stays in the secure chip (or the user's synced keychain) and cannot be read out.

messages.label: credential id, public key
messages.note: attestationObject: rp id hash, flags (user present, user verified, backup state), sign count, credential id, public key. Plus clientDataJSON: type, challenge, origin.

messages.label: Verify, save AccessKey
messages.note: Checks type webauthn.create, its own challenge, the origin, the rp id hash and the user-verified flag. Refuses a credential id it already has. Saves the row with kind = passkey, the backup-eligible and backup-state flags (synced or device-bound) and the authenticator's make for the label. Sends a security email.

messages.label: Protected action
messages.note: Part 2 - confirm, every time a feature asks. Same steps whoever the verifier is.

messages.label: challenge
messages.note: Made by the verifier: hash of (verifier id, purpose, random nonce, expiry). Single use, 5 minutes. Binding the purpose stops a relay from reusing the answer for something else.

messages.label: Sign with private key
messages.note: Signs authenticatorData + SHA-256(clientDataJSON). So the signature covers the challenge, the page's origin, the rp id, the user-verified flag and the sign count.

messages.label: Get user's access keys
messages.note: Skipped when the verifier already pinned them: a machine does, through set_machine_access_key() in the Python SDK.

messages.label: verify_assertion()
messages.note: Shared pure function, chosen by the key's kind. For kind passkey: signature valid for a known public key, challenge is its own and unused, origin and rp id are the hub's, user verified, sign count not going backwards.

messages.label: confirmed
messages.note: What happens next (a 1-hour window, one action) is the feature's business, not this piece's.
